decision: The Week 6 integration QA records authorization and session refresh as separate executable checks, then verifies their fail-closed boundary scenarios rather than adding a duplicate orchestration layer. This preserves the responsibilities of the refresh coordinator and the authorization service while making their observable protections reproducible.
alternatives: Add a new integration implementation that couples profile authorization to SessionRefreshCoordinator and test that new layer.
Reuse the existing focused authorization and public refresh suites, recording only executed nominal, boundary, and failure observations.
Rely only on the public Week 6 suite and omit the application-level authorization checks.
tradeoff: Focused suites give precise ownership and deterministic diagnosis for session and permission failures, but do not simulate a networked end-to-end UI flow. Adding a coupling layer solely for QA would broaden the product surface, duplicate tested behavior, and risk changing the work already integrated from the other contributors.

verification.evidence: 7/7 public refresh tests passed, including concurrent 401 coalescing, one retry, failed/invalid refresh, stale generation, and logout invalidation.
3/3 suites and 26/26 authorization tests passed; denied operations were asserted before repository mutation.
Controlled backend self-test passed for roles, reassignment conflict, lost response, idempotency, evidence, and geocoding.
